item.title: $100 Million Bet on Venezuelan Fintech Cashea Draws Global Investors
item.description: Cashea, Venezuela’s largest financial technology company, has raised $100 million across two financing rounds, as global investors bet it can grow in a market where lending has been constrained for years.

item.title: Kalshi Seeks Approval for Perpetual Futures Tied to Gold, Silver
item.description: Kalshi Inc. is seeking approval to expand precious-metals trading on its platform with a popular type of derivative that never expires for gold, silver and platinum.

item.title: London’s 24-Hour Trading Is Unlikely to Revive Market, GAM Says
item.description: The London Stock Exchange’s plan to introduce nearly 24-hour trading for equities may fall short of reviving the bourse’s fortunes, the head of GAM Investments’ global equities team said.

item.title: Nigeria Holds Interest Rates as War Stokes Inflation Fears
item.description: Nigeria’s central bank held interest rates as expected to curtail price pressures from the Iran war, which it described as the biggest risk to its outlook.

item.title: Indian Refiners Halt Iraq Oil Loadings as Hormuz Risks Escalate
item.description: Two Indian state-run refiners have suspended crude oil loadings from Iraq as mounting security risks in the Strait of Hormuz make it increasingly difficult to ensure safety of vessels, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: OpenAI’s Agents Reach 10 Million Users After ChatGPT Work Debut
item.description: OpenAI has seen a sharp uptick in demand for its artificial intelligence agents since its recent release of ChatGPT Work, providing new momentum in its bid to keep pace with rival Anthropic PBC.

item.title: Short Sellers Ramp Up Bets Against HelloFresh’s Debut Bond
item.description: Bets against HelloFresh SE’s debut bond, issued only three weeks ago, have surged after its trading got off to a rocky start earlier this month.

item.title: Garmin Debuts $200 Screenless Fitness Band in Challenge to Whoop
item.description: Garmin Ltd. introduced a $200 screenless fitness tracker, becoming the latest company to enter a segment popularized by Whoop Inc.

item.title: Colombia, Peru Send Early Policy Signs to Extend Election Rally
item.description: Investors are finding fresh reasons to buy Colombian and Peruvian assets as the countries’ newly elected presidents deliver early signals that their market-friendly agendas will translate into policy overhaul.

item.title: InMobi Appoints JPMorgan, Jefferies for Nearly $1 Billion IPO
item.description: InMobi Pte has appointed four banks for an initial public offering over the next few months to raise about $1 billion for the Indian mobile advertising company.

item.title: Biotech IPOs Outperform AI Listings, Leading US Market in 2026
item.description: The biotechnology sector is stealing the US IPO market thunder from artificial intelligence-related listings, delivering standout returns as bankers line up a steady stream of summer debuts.

item.title: Nasdaq 100 Soars as Chipmaker Rebound Overshadows Iran War
item.description: The Nasdaq 100 Index advanced on Tuesday as a rebound in chipmakers at the center of the artificial-intelligence trade overshadowed the re-escalation in the US-Iran war.

item.title: Samsung Debuts AI-Powered Health Assistant, Joining Packed Market
item.description: Samsung Electronics Co. is rolling out a new AI-powered assistant that acts as a virtual health companion, joining a growing number of tech companies using chatbots to deliver personalized wellness insights to its users.Samsung Health Assistant pulls in data from the user’s Galaxy smartphone, smartwatch or smart ring, the company said Tuesday. The firm also announced a series of other features coming to its health platform, particularly around heart metrics.

item.title: Saudi Crude Flow From Red Sea Hit Record Before Houthi Warning
item.description: Saudi Arabia exported record volumes of crude oil from terminals on the Red Sea in the days and weeks before the Houthis said they would block the nation’s shipments.

item.title: Bessent Says US to Scrutinize Chinese AI Models for IP Theft
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the US will carefully examine open source artificial intelligence models from China for signs of intellectual property theft, amid concerns that a new wave of lower-cost Chinese competitors may sweep aside the top American models.

item.title: Kenya Reveals 30-Year Plan to Reach Developed-Economy Status
item.description: Kenya unveiled a 30-year plan to transform the East African nation into a high-income industrialized economy by focusing on increased farm productivity, expanded export-oriented manufacturing, and deeper technology and innovation.

item.title: Chinese Oil Tanker U-Turns in Red Sea After Houthi Attack Threat
item.description: A very large crude carrier has made a U-turn in the southern Red Sea after warnings from Houthi rebels in Yemen that they would target ships heading to or from Saudi ports.

item.title: Hungary Cuts Rates for Second Month as Inflation Stays Soft
item.description: Hungary’s central bank lowered borrowing costs for a second straight month as subdued inflation allows policymakers to press ahead with a monetary easing cycle.

item.title: China’s World AI Conference and TSMC’s Arizona Investment Mark Wins for Leaders
item.description: As China convenes a global AI conference, Arizona receives more investment

item.title: Economic Momentum Flips From Blessing to Curse for S&P 500 Bulls
item.description: Strong economic momentum is a double-edged sword for US equity traders. Solid growth is an earnings tailwind. But let it run too hot, and it turns from blessing to curse.

item.title: Shale Trades Go-Go Days of Growth for Output Creep
item.description: US drillers are letting production rise again — just not the way they used to.

item.title: Wall Street Talks Up Carry Trade as Returns Soar Most in Decades
item.description: One of the most enduring foreign-exchange bets is off to its best run in decades as surprisingly muted volatility across asset classes has investors piling into carry trades.

item.title: Victoria Debt Deal Faces Opposition From HSBC Bank
item.description: UK carpet maker Victoria Plc.’s bid to restructure its balance sheet is facing resistance from HSBC Holdings Plc, a holder of the company’s bonds.

item.title: Tether’s Three-Way Crypto Deal Is Called Off, Mallers Steps Down
item.description: A proposed merger of three crypto firms has been scrapped, with one of their leaders stepping down and another consolidating power across the Tether-backed franchise.

item.title: China’s Double Moonshot Moment in the AI Tech Race
item.description: China is closing the technology gap on both AI models and the chips that make them possible

item.title: Trump and Canada tariff threat
item.description: The move would hit about $20 billion worth of Canadian imports to the US

item.title: Data Centers on Track to Suck Up a Fifth of US Power Use by 2035
item.description: Data centers in the US will account for about 20% of the nation’s electricity consumption in 2035, up from 5.9% today, according to BloombergNEF.

item.title: IEA Warns Mideast Hostilities Are Increasing Oil Supply Concerns
item.description: The International Energy Agency said it’s “closely monitoring the situation in oil markets” as escalating hostilities in the Middle East increase the concerns over security of supplies.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Stop Piping Oil to Black Sea After Tanker Attacks
item.description: Kazakhstan is set to stop piping crude to a port on Russia’s Black Sea coast after a spate of attacks on tankers that’s jeopardizing the landlocked Asian country’s ability to produce oil.

item.title: Carlyle in Talks to Hand ESG Consulting Firm Over to Bridgepoint
item.description: Carlyle Group Inc. is in talks to hand the keys of sustainability consultancy Anthesis Group over to its private credit lender Bridgepoint Group Plc, people with knowledge of the matter said.
